cities.route: I-80 West: New Jersey > Pennsylvania mountains > Ohio > south of Chicago > Iowa > Nebraska > Wyoming > Salt Lake City
cities.profile: The densest start in the game (about 29,300 people per square mile), so the outbreak is worst here on Day 1. The player has to escape the most infected city fast, about 280 miles a day. Food and water are easy to find in the first two days and scarce on the plains, so stocking up early matters. Wyoming's deep cold slows the infected but punishes anyone without shelter.

scenarios.title: Bridges Close at Noon
scenarios.text: An emergency alert screams from every phone: all bridges and tunnels out of Manhattan close at NOON. It's 8 a.m. Your neighbor's door bursts open down the hall, and someone is screaming.

options.text: Raid the corner store for water and snacks, then run for the bridge
options.note: The supplies help a lot later, but the store is chaos and the player barely beats the closure.

options.text: Push into Penn Station for the last train west
options.note: Trains might run, but packed stations are the worst place in the highest-infection city in the game.

options.text: Drive your car toward the Holland Tunnel
options.note: Looks fastest, but tunnels jam solid with no side exits, and the infected move between stalled cars.

options.text: Grab your go-bag and walk fast to the George Washington Bridge
options.note: Walking beats gridlock, and the GW Bridge leads straight to I-80 West. The player makes it out with hours to spare.

scenarios.title: Fort Lee, 24°F
scenarios.text: You crossed into New Jersey. It's dark by 4:45 p.m. and 24°F. An empty diner, an SUV idling with its door wide open, and people waving from an apartment lobby.

options.text: Join the people waving from the lobby
options.note: Warm and friendly, but strangers are unpredictable. A tense but safe night.

options.text: Break into the diner, barricade the doors, and eat
options.note: A gas stove for heat, a walk-in fridge of food, and bottled drinks. One door to watch.

options.text: Jump in the idling SUV and go
options.note: Looks like a jackpot, but the owner turned in the back seat. An attack from behind.

options.text: Keep walking in the dark toward I-80
options.note: Miles gained, but ice and darkness mean falls and surprise attacks.

scenarios.title: The Wall of Cars
scenarios.text: I-80 through the Pocono Mountains is a frozen wall of abandoned cars. Snow is falling hard. A tow truck sits with its keys in it, and a car dealership's showroom glows nearby.

options.text: Follow fresh tire tracks leading off the highway
options.note: Looks smart (someone made it through!), but the tracks lead to a raider camp.

options.text: Take the tow truck
options.note: Looks slow and loud, but it can shove stalled cars aside and plow through snowdrifts. The perfect jam-buster.

options.text: Grab a new car from the dealership showroom
options.note: Looks like the obvious move, but dozens of people sheltered there and turned.

options.text: Ride a bike from a shop along the shoulder
options.note: It gets past the jam, but biking in a snowstorm is brutal and the player carries little.

scenarios.title: The Hunting Cabin
scenarios.text: Snow Shoe, Pennsylvania. A truck stop roars with a generator and bright lights. Up a dark trail, smoke rises from a hunting cabin's chimney.

options.text: Hike to the hunting cabin
options.note: An old hunter shares venison jerky and melts snow on his wood stove for drinking water. Quiet and safe.

options.text: Sleep in the sporting goods store downtown
options.note: Good gear, but the broken windows mean a freezing night.

options.text: Head for the truck stop with power
options.note: Electricity seems great, but the noise and light pull in every infected for miles.

options.text: Keep driving the mountain grades through the night
options.note: Gains miles, but black ice on the grades causes crashes.

scenarios.title: The Boy at the Rest Stop
scenarios.text: At an Ohio rest stop, a boy about ten runs toward you, crying. His dad is "sick" and won't wake up in their fogged-up car. Something inside the car bangs against the window.

options.text: Pull the boy away and leave the car shut
options.note: The dad has turned. The boy isn't bitten, and he becomes a loyal companion. Sets BOY_ALLY.

options.text: Open the car door to check on his dad
options.note: The dad lunges out. The worst outcome.

options.text: Drive away without stopping
options.note: Safe from the dad, but the story and the player's morale take a hit.

options.text: Give the boy food and directions to the next town, then leave
options.note: Safe for the player, but they lose a potential ally and some food.

scenarios.title: Lake-Effect Whiteout
scenarios.text: Near Toledo, lake-effect snow off Lake Erie turns everything white. A hospital with a red cross banner glows to your left. A big-box store with a roof ladder sits to your right.

options.text: Shelter in a lakeside boathouse
options.note: Quiet, but freezing wind off the lake all night.

options.text: Seek help at the hospital
options.note: A red cross looks safe, but hospitals were ground zero. Overrun.

options.text: Drive through the whiteout
options.note: Zero visibility. Maybe the player makes it, maybe they end up in a ditch.

options.text: Climb the ladder to the big-box store roof and drop in through the hatch
options.note: Zombies can't climb ladders. Inside: shelves of canned food and cases of water.

scenarios.title: The Convoy
scenarios.text: South of Chicago, National Guard trucks race west, sirens blaring. A soldier leans out: "Get in! Secure camp in Chicago!" Behind the convoy, a crowd of infected is chasing the noise.

options.text: Follow the convoy at a distance
options.note: The player might pick up dropped supplies, or drive into the crowd chasing the trucks.

options.text: Jump in and ride the convoy into Chicago
options.note: Soldiers look like safety, but the camp is in a city of 2.7 million and already falling.

options.text: Wave them on, then ask the last truck for fuel and water
options.note: Soldiers toss the player water bottles and a road report showing which roads west are clear.

options.text: Hide in a ditch until the convoy and the crowd pass
options.note: No reward, but no risk either.

scenarios.title: The Jackknifed Semi
scenarios.text: A jackknifed grocery semi blocks the bridge over the Illinois River. The ice on the river below looks solid, but you can hear water moving under it. Something shuffles inside the trailer.

options.text: Drive across the frozen river
options.note: Moving rivers rarely freeze solid. The ice gives way.

options.text: Backtrack 20 miles to the next bridge
options.note: Safe, but it costs fuel and hours.

options.text: Find the keys in the cab and move the semi
options.note: The keys are in the cab, the shuffling is a loose pallet, and the trailer is full of food.

options.text: Climb over the semi on foot with your gear
options.note: The player gets across, but tears their arm on jagged metal. Sets SCRATCHED.

scenarios.title: The Bite Check
scenarios.text: At the Mississippi River bridge into Iowa, soldiers with rifles are screening everyone for bites. Your travel partner has a fresh scratch they swear came from a fence. The line is moving fast.

options.text: Look for another crossing upriver
options.note: Safe, but it costs half a day.

options.text: Hide the scratch under a coat
options.note: Seems clever, but soldiers search everyone. Getting caught means being detained at gunpoint.

options.text: Leave your partner behind and cross alone
options.note: The player crosses safely but loses an ally. A heavy choice.

options.text: Be honest and show the scratch
options.note: A medic confirms it's from a fence. Honesty gets the player through, and they get a medical check and water.

scenarios.title: The Farmhouse Dinner
scenarios.text: In Iowa, an elderly couple invites you in for hot stew. They seem kind. A shotgun leans by their door, and you hear something moving in the barn.

options.text: Steal their truck while they sleep
options.note: Their son is on guard in the barn. Shots fired.

options.text: Thank them and sleep in your car
options.note: Safe and polite, but cold and hungry.

options.text: Accept, but keep watch in shifts
options.note: Kindness plus caution. A hot meal, filled water jugs and a safe night. The barn noise is their cow.

options.text: Accept and sleep soundly
options.note: Probably fine, but no one is on watch if something goes wrong.

scenarios.title: Bailey Yard
scenarios.text: North Platte, Nebraska: the world's largest rail yard. A rail worker has a locomotive running and says he can take it 200 miles west. Infected are pouring out of the yard office toward you.

options.text: Climb aboard the locomotive with him now
options.note: Sounds crazy, but tracks aren't jammed like highways. Over 200 fast miles, and he shares his lunch.

options.text: Try to drive another locomotive yourself
options.note: The player has no idea how. Derailment.

options.text: Stay on I-80 and drive away
options.note: Safe and steady, but the player misses the shortcut.

options.text: Grab food from the yard cafeteria first
options.note: Food inside, but the infected are coming from that direction.

scenarios.title: The Air Force Base
scenarios.text: In Cheyenne, the air base gates hang open. The wind howls at 60 mph. A helicopter sits on the pad, and a fuel depot and mess hall are lit by emergency lights.

options.text: Take the helicopter
options.note: Exciting, but the player can't fly, and nobody flies in 60 mph winds.

options.text: Search the armory
options.note: Weapons help, but it's been picked over.

options.text: Sleep in the barracks
options.note: Warm beds, but the soldiers sheltered there may have turned.

options.text: Fill up at the fuel depot and raid the mess hall
options.note: A full tank, military rations and jugs of water for the empty stretch ahead.

scenarios.title: Frozen Solid
scenarios.text: It's -15°F near Rock Springs, Wyoming. The infected along I-80 are frozen stiff and barely moving. Your gas is low, and the only station is in the middle of town.

options.text: Stop to destroy the frozen infected one by one
options.note: It works, but the player is exposed to frostbite for an hour.

options.text: Drive into town now while they're sluggish and fill up
options.note: The cold rule from our infection model: extreme cold slows the infected way down. Use it.

options.text: Coast to the next town on fumes
options.note: Probably okay, but the player arrives with an empty tank.

options.text: Build a campfire next to the frozen ones to warm up
options.note: They look dead, but the fire thaws them out.

scenarios.title: The Final Gate
scenarios.text: You reach the Salt Lake City safe zone at night. Guards order everyone to strip off their coats for a bite check in the freezing wind. A stranger beside you refuses and starts shouting.

options.text: Try to keep a hidden knife
options.note: If the guards find it, the player is detained and questioned.

options.text: Wait outside until morning when things calm down
options.note: Probably fine, but it's one more freezing night with the infected around.

options.text: Cooperate fully and step away from the stranger
options.note: The player is clean and walks in. Victory.

options.text: Demand the guards let the stranger in without a check
options.note: Guards lock the gates on both of them.

branches.title: The Chase
branches.text: Your bad call drew a pack of infected, and now you're on foot, sprinting through snowy suburban backyards. They're 30 feet behind you and closing.

options.text: Climb trash cans onto a garage roof and kick the cans away
options.note: The infected can't climb. The player waits on the roof until the pack drifts off, then sneaks back.

options.text: Dive into the thick bushes and hold perfectly still
options.note: Looks like a smart hiding spot, but winter bushes have no leaves. The infected see the player right through the bare branches.

options.text: Jump the backyard fences one after another
options.note: Fences slow the infected, but the player snags their arm on chain-link going over the third one. Sets the SCRATCHED flag, and the Aching Arm callback plays 2 scenarios later.

options.text: Circle back to your vehicle the long way around the block
options.note: It works, but it takes an hour and the player is exhausted for the next scenario.

branches.title: Coal Country Back Roads
branches.text: Your gamble sent you off I-80 onto twisting back roads through old coal and steel towns. One tiny town has blocked its main street with two school buses. A man with a megaphone shouts, "State your business!"

options.text: Wait until dark and sneak in for supplies
options.note: Could find supplies, but small-town watchmen know every shadow.

options.text: Turn around and find your own way back to I-80
options.note: Safe, but it costs most of the morning.

options.text: Shout back honestly: you're passing through and can trade
options.note: Small towns respect honesty. The mayor trades the player gas for news and shows them a shortcut back to I-80.

options.text: Drive around the barricade through the cemetery
options.note: The town sees it as an attack. Warning shots, and the player is chased off.

branches.title: Stranded in the Snow
branches.text: Your car slides off the highway into a deep snowbank on the open plains. It won't budge. It's -8°F, and a farmhouse light glows about three miles away.

options.text: Walk to the farmhouse light
options.note: Looks like the obvious move, but three miles at -8°F in the dark leads to hypothermia, and lights on flat land are farther than they look.

options.text: Wave down the next set of headlights
options.note: Could be help. Could be raiders who now know the player is stuck.

options.text: Stay with the car, tie a bright cloth to the antenna, and run the engine 10 minutes an hour
options.note: Looks like giving up, but staying with the vehicle is the top winter survival rule. A plow driver spots the cloth by morning.

options.text: Dig the tires out using a hubcap as a shovel
options.note: It works after two hours of exhausting work.

branches.title: The Voice on the CB Radio
branches.text: Your risky choice put you near a lonely weather station on the plains. Your CB radio crackles: a meteorologist inside says she'll share the storm forecast in exchange for food.

options.text: Thank her and keep driving
options.note: Safe, but the player drives blind into the weather.

options.text: Invite her to come with you to Salt Lake City
options.note: A smart ally, but she's injured and slows the player down.

options.text: Drive over and trade a can of food for the forecast
options.note: She shows the player a calm-weather window to cross the mountains. Code option: skip one bad-weather penalty later.

options.text: Hand over all your food for the forecast
options.note: Info is useful, but the player is now starving for the last days.

callbacks.title: The Aching Arm
callbacks.text: Two scenarios ago you scraped your arm. Now it throbs under your sleeve, red and warm to the touch. Your companion glances at it. Was it the fence, or something else?

options.text: Hide it under your sleeve and say nothing
options.note: Looks like the way to avoid panic, but the scrape gets infected, and when the companion finds out, trust is broken.

options.text: Clean it with soap and water, bandage it, and tell your companion to watch you for a day
options.note: Truth: it's from the chain-link fence, not a bite. Cleaning stops a real infection, and honesty keeps the companion's trust.

options.text: Pour alcohol from the first-aid kit on it and keep moving
options.note: It disinfects the wound, but stings badly, and the companion still worries.

options.text: Ask your companion to check for teeth marks
options.note: They find none, but now they're nervous around the player for the rest of the trip.

callbacks.title: The Boy's Secret
callbacks.text: The boy from the rest stop has been quiet. Tonight he finally whispers that his dad got bitten at a gas station two days before you found them, and he's scared he's sick too.

options.text: Leave him at the next town just to be safe
options.note: He isn't infected. Abandoning a child is a heavy story penalty.

options.text: Tie his wrists "just for tonight"
options.note: Looks cautious, but it terrifies him, and he runs away during the night.

options.text: Gently check him for bites and promise you'll keep him safe
options.note: No bites anywhere. He's just scared. He becomes a loyal helper who spots danger first.

options.text: Comfort him, but don't check
options.note: He feels better, but the player never knows for sure.

cities.route: Mass Pike > Hartford > Hudson River > Pennsylvania I-81 > Shenandoah Valley > Tennessee I-40 > Memphis > Arkansas > Oklahoma > Texas Panhandle > Albuquerque
cities.profile: A dense start (about 13,900 people per square mile). The route heads south and gets warmer, but the Oklahoma ice and the Panhandle blizzard hit hard late. Water is the big problem in the dry New Mexico high desert on the final day, so filling up before then matters.

scenarios.title: Nor'easter Lockdown
scenarios.text: A nor'easter is burying Boston in snow. The news says the airport is running evacuation flights. Screams echo from the street, and your building's front door just shattered.

options.text: Run for the airport evacuation flights
options.note: Sounds official, but the airport is reached through tunnels and is mobbed. Overrun by noon.

options.text: Take the back stairs to your car and drive west on the Mass Pike now
options.note: Get out early before the roads clog. The Pike leads straight to the route west.

options.text: Fill every pot with tap water, then shelter in the basement
options.note: Good water supply, but the city's infection is climbing fast.

options.text: Steal a boat across the harbor
options.note: Out of the crowds, but rough winter seas.

scenarios.title: The Fire Station
scenarios.text: Snow stops you in Worcester. A fire station sits with its bay doors shut. A college dorm has lights on. Down the street, a hospital is surrounded by people.

options.text: Go to the hospital for help
options.note: Hospitals are where the infected were taken. Overrun.

options.text: Get into the fire station
options.note: Medical kits, heavy coats, a water tank and steel bay doors. Firefighters are built for emergencies.

options.text: Sleep in an abandoned church
options.note: Quiet, but its big windows are easy to break.

options.text: Knock at the college dorm
options.note: The students share pizza, but they're disorganized and loud.

scenarios.title: The Radio Host
scenarios.text: Hartford is dark except for one radio tower. A DJ is broadcasting, begging travelers to help restart his failing generator. Infected are gathering at the station's fence.

options.text: Ask him to broadcast that you're looking for allies
options.note: Allies might hear, and so might raiders.

options.text: Raid the station's supplies while he's distracted
options.note: He sees everything and broadcasts the player's car description to everyone listening.

options.text: Help him fix the generator
options.note: He shares road reports for the whole route and broadcasts warnings ahead. A great ally. Sets DJ_ALLY.

options.text: Keep driving and listen while his signal lasts
options.note: Free information without helping, but the broadcast dies within the hour.

scenarios.title: The Abandoned Checkpoint
scenarios.text: The bridge over the Hudson River has an abandoned army checkpoint: sandbags, bodies, and a military Humvee with the keys in it. One of the bodies twitches.

options.text: Turn back to find another bridge 40 miles away
options.note: A huge waste of time and fuel in the snow.

options.text: Drive straight through the checkpoint
options.note: Safe crossing, no bonus.

options.text: Search the bodies for weapons
options.note: Some aren't fully dead.

options.text: Take the Humvee and drive
options.note: Looks like overkill, but it's armored, four-wheel drive, and stocked with ready-to-eat meals.

scenarios.title: Nuclear Sirens
scenarios.text: Near the Three Mile Island nuclear plant, sirens wail. The radio warns of a possible radiation leak. The wind blows from the south.

options.text: Keep heading southwest, windows up, air on recirculate
options.note: Moves against the wind, away from where the plume is headed.

options.text: Shelter in a basement for a day
options.note: Actually the official advice, but it costs a full day.

options.text: Break into a pharmacy for iodine pills
options.note: Iodine protects the thyroid, but break-ins are dangerous.

options.text: Detour north to get away from the plant
options.note: Feels smart, but wind from the south carries radiation north, right where the player would go.

scenarios.title: The Caverns
scenarios.text: In Virginia's Shenandoah Valley, you reach a huge underground cave that stays about 54°F all year. The visitor center has vending machines. You hear moaning in the dark tunnels below.

options.text: Barricade yourself in the visitor center
options.note: Warm air from the caves, vending machine food and drinks, and lockable doors.

options.text: Go deep into the caves to sleep where it's warm
options.note: Warm, but pitch-black, easy to get lost, and the moaning is the infected.

options.text: Drive the valley at night
options.note: More miles, but deer and infected on dark roads.

options.text: Sleep in your car in the lot
options.note: Cold, but okay.

scenarios.title: The Hitchhiker
scenarios.text: Near Knoxville, a hitchhiker with a guitar case waves you down in freezing rain. He says he knows a back way around Nashville's gridlock. He's soaked and shaking.

options.text: Pick him up but check the guitar case first
options.note: It holds a real guitar and a map. He's honest, and his shortcut saves hours. Sets HITCHHIKER.

options.text: Pick him up with no questions
options.note: He's honest, but the player got lucky. Sets HITCHHIKER.

options.text: Take his guitar case and drive off
options.note: He was telling the truth. Bad karma, and the player loses the shortcut.

options.text: Toss him a water bottle and drive on
options.note: Kind, and no risk, but no shortcut either.

scenarios.title: Music City
scenarios.text: Nashville's honky-tonks are still blaring music on a loop. The noise has drawn every infected downtown. A pharmacy sits dark two blocks from the music.

options.text: Head toward the music to look for survivors
options.note: It's not survivors. It's an automatic playlist and a crowd of infected.

options.text: Wait outside the city until dawn
options.note: Safe.

options.text: Raid the pharmacy while they're distracted
options.note: Medicine and bottled water, but the player is in the middle of the city.

options.text: Take the bypass around downtown while the music distracts them
options.note: Use the noise as cover.

scenarios.title: The Gap in the Bridge
scenarios.text: The I-40 bridge over the Mississippi at Memphis has a 10-foot gap blown out by the military. Infected are wandering onto the bridge behind you.

options.text: Floor it and try to jump the gap
options.note: This isn't a movie. The car falls into the river.

options.text: Use the other bridge one mile south
options.note: An easy detour. Always look for alternatives.

options.text: Cross by boat
options.note: Strong currents and freezing water.

options.text: Wait for army engineers to fix it
options.note: They're working on it, but it takes days.

scenarios.title: The Church Rule
scenarios.text: In Little Rock, a church group offers a hot meal and shelter, but everyone must hand over their weapons at the door. Inside, you smell soup.

options.text: Hand over your main weapon and respect the rules
options.note: Builds trust. Soup, filled water jugs, and the weapon is returned in the morning.

options.text: Threaten them to let you in armed
options.note: They're armed too. A bad outcome.

options.text: Refuse and sleep in a laundromat down the street
options.note: The player keeps their weapons, but it's a cold, glass-front building.

options.text: Hand over all your weapons
options.note: Probably safe, but the player is defenseless if things go wrong.

scenarios.title: The Nation's Checkpoint
scenarios.text: At the Oklahoma line, Cherokee Nation tribal police run a well-organized checkpoint with medical tents and a water truck.

options.text: Follow their rules and accept a medical check
options.note: Organized communities are the safest. Medical care, water and road intel.

options.text: Sneak around the checkpoint
options.note: Caught trespassing. The player loses their trust and help.

options.text: Offer a trade and pass through quickly
options.note: Fair and quick, but no medical check.

options.text: Ask to join them permanently
options.note: They might say yes, but the player abandons the mission.

scenarios.title: Steakhouse in a Blizzard
scenarios.text: A blizzard hits Amarillo. A famous roadside steakhouse has lights on and smoke rising. Someone's grilling, and the smell is incredible.

options.text: Sleep in a grain silo
options.note: Out of the wind, but cold and hungry.

options.text: Drive on through the blizzard
options.note: High winds on the flat plains. Whiteout.

options.text: Sneak in through the kitchen
options.note: Mistaken for a raider. Shots fired.

options.text: Knock and offer a trade
options.note: Survivors are cooking all the meat before it spoils. Hot food and a warm night.

scenarios.title: The Blue Hole
scenarios.text: In Santa Rosa, New Mexico, a natural spring 80 feet deep steams in the 15°F air. The water is 64°F. The high desert ahead is bone dry.

options.text: Skip it to save time
options.note: The player is low on water. Bad later.

options.text: Refill every water container you have
options.note: Clean water that doesn't freeze, and the desert ahead has none.

options.text: Fill one bottle and keep moving
options.note: A little water, quickly.

options.text: Swim in it to warm up
options.note: Feels warm for a moment, but wet clothes at 15°F mean hypothermia.

scenarios.title: The Gate Interview
scenarios.text: At the Albuquerque safe zone gate, guards ask what skills you have to offer. Behind you, the infected are gathering in the dark.

options.text: Lie and say you're a doctor
options.note: Sounds like a VIP pass, but they put the player to work treating the infected.

options.text: Refuse to give up your vehicle
options.note: The player gets in after a long, cold argument.

options.text: Tell them your real skills
options.note: Honesty. They place the player where they're useful. Victory.

options.text: Offer your supplies
options.note: Accepted, but they wanted skills more than supplies.

branches.title: The Fire Escape
branches.text: Your bad choice sent you into an apartment building, and infected are coming up the stairwell. You're on the third floor with an icy fire escape outside the window.

options.text: Barricade the apartment door with the couch
options.note: It holds for a few hours, but the player loses most of the day.

options.text: Hide in a closet and wait for them to leave
options.note: Looks safe, but the infected hear breathing. A dead end.

options.text: Jump from the fire escape into a snow-covered dumpster
options.note: Soft landing or a twisted ankle. Fifty-fifty.

options.text: Climb up the fire escape to the roof
options.note: The infected are slow on ladders. The player crosses to the next building's roof and comes down the far side.

branches.title: Wrong Turn into the Mountains
branches.text: Your risky detour put you on a winding road into the mountains. You find an old summer camp with log cabins, a dining hall, and smoke from one chimney.

options.text: Call out from the road and wait for an answer
options.note: A camp caretaker answers. He gives the player a warm cabin and a map back to the interstate.

options.text: Walk into the dining hall without calling out
options.note: A group of infected was locked inside the dining hall, and the player opens the door on them.

options.text: Turn around and find the highway
options.note: Safe, but lost hours.

options.text: Search the empty cabins for supplies
options.note: Some blankets and food, but the player loses time and could meet trouble.

branches.title: Lost on the Back Roads
branches.text: Your bad choice put you on twisty rural back roads with a quarter tank. A family on a porch is passing a jar of homemade liquor and offers you some to "warm up."

options.text: Politely decline and ask for directions back to the interstate
options.note: They point the player to a gravel shortcut and trade a gas can.

options.text: Ask to sleep in their barn
options.note: Friendly, but the barn is close to the woods where the infected wander.

options.text: Find your own way back
options.note: Hours lost on the twisting roads.

options.text: Drink the liquor to warm up
options.note: Feels warm, but alcohol makes the body lose heat faster. A real winter myth that leads to hypothermia.

branches.title: Old Highway Ghost Town
branches.text: Your gamble took you off the interstate onto an old two-lane highway and into a ghost town. An abandoned gas station still has fuel in its old pumps, and a hand crank.

options.text: Skip it and head back to the interstate
options.note: Safe, but the player is still low on fuel.

options.text: Search the old motel for supplies
options.note: Some useful items, but a family of infected took shelter there.

options.text: Light a lantern to see the pump better
options.note: An open flame near old fuel pumps. Fire.

options.text: Hand-crank the old pump to fill up
options.note: It works. A full tank with zero crowds.

callbacks.title: A Voice on the Radio
callbacks.text: The radio crackles. It's the DJ from Hartford whose generator you fixed: "To the traveler who helped me, raiders on I-81 are faking car crashes to stop drivers. Don't stop for wrecks!"

options.text: Thank him on the radio and plan to drive past any wrecks
options.note: The player avoids a raider trap later. Code option: cancel one future raider penalty.

options.text: Note the warning and keep going
options.note: Fine.

options.text: Ask him if he knows any safe route around I-81
options.note: He gives a longer back-road route. Safer from raiders, but slower.

options.text: Broadcast your exact location to thank him
options.note: Raiders listen to the radio too.

callbacks.title: The Bleeding Hand
callbacks.text: The hitchhiker you picked up two scenarios ago has a bandage on his hand that's soaking through with blood. He says he cut it on a broken guitar string.

options.text: Look at the cut yourself, then clean and rebandage it
options.note: It's a clean straight cut from a guitar string. Not a bite. Trust grows.

options.text: Kick him out of the car without checking
options.note: He was telling the truth, and he's now alone in the cold.

options.text: Hand him the first-aid kit and keep driving
options.note: Fine, but the player never sees the wound.

options.text: Make him sit in the back seat with his hands tied
options.note: Looks careful, but it destroys trust, and he leaves at the next stop.

cities.route: I-70 West: Ohio > Indianapolis > St. Louis > Kansas City > Kansas plains > Denver > Rocky Mountain tunnel > Utah desert > I-15 > Las Vegas
cities.profile: Mid-size cold city. Bridges and farms early, the empty plains in the middle, then the hardest stretch of any route: the Rockies in winter and 106 miles of Utah desert with no services. Food and water must be stocked before Day 6.

scenarios.title: City of Bridges
scenarios.text: The Fort Pitt Tunnel is jammed solid, and horns are blaring. In the rearview mirror, you see infected climbing over cars toward the tunnel entrance.

options.text: Ride the incline railway up Mount Washington to hide
options.note: Great view, but the player could get trapped up top.

options.text: Stay in the tunnel traffic
options.note: It's moving slowly, but when the infected reach the tunnel, nobody can get out.

options.text: Leave the car and cross the West End Bridge on foot
options.note: Walks past the jam. A car with keys and a cooler of drinks waits on the far side.

options.text: Shelter in the university's 42-story tower
options.note: Tall and defensible, but the player is still in the city.

scenarios.title: Horse-and-Buggy Country
scenarios.text: In eastern Ohio, an Amish family with no electricity seems untouched by the chaos. Their lanterns glow. Their dogs are barking at something in the dark field behind you.

options.text: Try to convince them to flee with you
options.note: They'll refuse, and the player loses time while the barking gets closer.

options.text: Camp at the edge of their farm
options.note: Safe, but cold, and the family stays wary.

options.text: Ask to stay in the barn and help with chores
options.note: They welcome help. Fresh bread, well water and a warm barn, and the dogs keep watch.

options.text: Steal one of their horses
options.note: They're peaceful, but the community turns the player away into the dark field.

scenarios.title: The Speedway
scenarios.text: At the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, race cars sit in the garages and a maintenance pickup is parked by the pits. Infected are stumbling across the infield toward you.

options.text: Take the four-wheel-drive pickup from the maintenance lot
options.note: Practical and built for winter. A case of water bottles is in the bed.

options.text: Fill gas cans with race fuel and leave
options.note: Works short term, but it isn't great for a normal engine.

options.text: Cut through downtown Indy to save time
options.note: A big city means more infected.

options.text: Take a race car
options.note: The fastest car around, but it has no heater, sits inches off the ground and is useless in snow.

scenarios.title: The Promise
scenarios.text: At a giant roadside cross in Effingham, Illinois, survivors huddle around fires. Their leader offers you fuel and food if you'll take a sick little girl to the Las Vegas safe zone.

options.text: Agree, but check her for bites first
options.note: No bites. It's an ear infection. Fuel, food and a grateful ally. Sets CARRYING_CHILD.

options.text: Take the supplies and leave without the child
options.note: They have guns, and the player has broken a promise.

options.text: Politely refuse
options.note: Safe, but no fuel and no food.

options.text: Agree without checking her
options.note: Probably fine, but risky. Sets CARRYING_CHILD.

scenarios.title: The Gateway Arch
scenarios.text: In St. Louis, a crowd of infected is crossing the main bridge toward you from the Missouri side. The 630-foot Gateway Arch towers overhead, and a tram runs to the top.

options.text: Drive north to the next bridge before the crowd reaches you
options.note: A short detour around the crowd.

options.text: Race across the main bridge before the crowd reaches the middle
options.note: Maybe the player makes it, maybe they plow into the crowd.

options.text: Pull back and wait on the Illinois side for an hour
options.note: Safe, but slow.

options.text: Ride the Arch tram to the top to wait it out
options.note: Looks unreachable, but if the power fails the player is trapped 630 feet up with one way out.

scenarios.title: Kansas City Barbecue
scenarios.text: In Kansas City, barbecue smoke drifts from a famous BBQ joint. Survivors are cooking all the meat before it spoils. A guard at the door says, "Trade or move on."

options.text: Trade a gas can for food and water
options.note: Hot food, water and a warning about the empty Kansas plains ahead.

options.text: Raid their meat locker
options.note: They see the player. A bad outcome.

options.text: Offer to join them for a few days
options.note: Comfortable and well fed, but the player loses time.

options.text: Keep driving through the city
options.note: Safe, but hungry.

scenarios.title: Last Gas for 80 Miles
scenarios.text: Western Kansas: 100 miles between towns. A sign says "Last Gas for 80 Miles." The station is dark, and its door is propped open with a body.

options.text: Siphon gas from abandoned cars outside
options.note: It works, but slowly.

options.text: Grab snacks from the front of the store
options.note: The food is still there, and so is whoever propped the door open.

options.text: Search the station's storage room for gas cans and bottled water
options.note: Gas cans and a pallet of bottled water are stored in back.

options.text: Keep going with half a tank
options.note: The player might not make it to the next town.

scenarios.title: Denver Lights
scenarios.text: Denver's skyline is lit. Someone has the power running. On the radio, a voice invites survivors to a stadium downtown.

options.text: Visit the stadium where survivors are gathering
options.note: Could be good. Could be a trap.

options.text: Head into the city to find the survivors
options.note: Light means people, and people mean infected.

options.text: Drive through the city at night
options.note: Possible, but crowded roads.

options.text: Camp in the foothills outside the city
options.note: Away from the crowds, with a clear creek for water.

scenarios.title: Into the Rockies
scenarios.text: I-70 climbs toward the Eisenhower Tunnel, over 11,000 feet up. Snow is falling hard. An avalanche warning flashes on a sign. Your tires are slipping.

options.text: Put on tire chains before climbing
options.note: Required by Colorado law in storms, and life-saving.

options.text: Wait at the bottom for the storm to pass
options.note: Safe, but it costs most of a day.

options.text: Take Loveland Pass over the top instead
options.note: Steep, icy and closed in storms.

options.text: Speed up the mountain to beat the snow
options.note: Black ice on curves. A crash.

scenarios.title: Hot Springs
scenarios.text: In Glenwood Springs, a giant natural hot spring pool steams in the 10°F night air. The spa building next to it is dark but unlocked.

options.text: Sleep in the spa building
options.note: Warm from the springs, with a snack bar and drinking fountains.

options.text: Rent a room in town above a closed shop
options.note: Fine, but no heat.

options.text: Soak in the hot springs
options.note: Feels amazing until the player gets out wet at 10°F. Sets SOAKED.

options.text: Drive through the canyon at night
options.note: Rockfall and ice on the canyon road, and nowhere to pull over.

scenarios.title: No Services for 106 Miles
scenarios.text: In Utah, I-70 enters the San Rafael Swell: 106 miles with no gas, no food and no help. A last rest stop has vending machines and a water fountain.

options.text: Drive in with half a tank
options.note: The player gets stranded in the desert.

options.text: Take a dirt road shortcut
options.note: Rough roads, and the player could get stuck.

options.text: Fill the water jugs only
options.note: Okay, but no food for the long drive.

options.text: Top off fuel, water and food before going in
options.note: Planning ahead is the only way to cross 106 empty miles.

scenarios.title: Desert Stars
scenarios.text: The Utah desert night drops to 15°F. A lonely gas station glows in the distance. Hidden canyons line the road.

options.text: Sleep under a rock overhang beside the road
options.note: Out of the wind, but visible from the highway.

options.text: Drive on with gas-station coffee
options.note: The player covers miles, but falling asleep at the wheel is a real danger.

options.text: Go to the gas station
options.note: Light in the middle of nowhere attracts every infected for miles.

options.text: Camp in a hidden canyon with your car
options.note: Hidden and out of the wind.

scenarios.title: The Gorge
scenarios.text: Near Las Vegas, the Virgin River Gorge is a narrow, curving canyon. A crashed bus blocks one lane, and its doors are banging open and shut.

options.text: Wait for someone else to move it
options.note: Nobody comes. Hours wasted.

options.text: Drive slowly around the bus in the clear lane
options.note: The lane is clear enough.

options.text: Climb the canyon wall on foot
options.note: Steep, icy rock with gear on the player's back.

options.text: Push the bus out of the way
options.note: It won't move, the player damages the car, and the noise wakes whatever is inside.

scenarios.title: The Vegas Lights
scenarios.text: Las Vegas! The safe zone is a fortified hotel complex. The Strip is lit up like nothing happened, and the infected are crowding the casinos.

options.text: Drive down the Strip to the safe zone
options.note: Looks like the direct path, but it's packed with the infected.

options.text: Wait until morning
options.note: One more night outside.

options.text: Signal the gate with your headlights
options.note: Guards see the player, and so do the infected.

options.text: Take the back road the radio described
options.note: The safe route to the gate. Victory.

branches.title: Overrun at the Rest Stop
branches.text: Your bad choice put you at a highway rest stop just as a crowd of infected stumbles out of the woods. You're 50 feet from your car.

options.text: Lock yourself in the restroom
options.note: Looks safe, but there's one door and no window. The player is trapped.

options.text: Sprint to your car, lock the doors, and drive off slowly through the lot
options.note: The car is the safest place. Slow driving avoids hitting anyone and spinning out on ice.

options.text: Hide in the rest stop's storage room
options.note: It works, but the player waits hours for them to leave.

options.text: Grab a tire iron and fight your way to the car
options.note: The player could make it. Or get bitten.

branches.title: The Frozen Caves
branches.text: Your gamble took you off I-70 into a state park with frozen waterfalls and giant rock caves. A group of hikers has camped inside a huge recess cave.

options.text: Climb the icy cliff for a better view
options.note: Frozen cliffs. A fall.

options.text: Join the hikers and share a fire
options.note: They're friendly and know every back road west.

options.text: Spend the night alone in a smaller cave
options.note: Quiet, but unknown, and the player is alone.

options.text: Thank them and head back to I-70
options.note: Safe.

branches.title: Runaway Mountain Brakes
branches.text: Your bad choice has you coming down a steep Colorado mountain grade when your brakes overheat and stop working. A sign flashes: "Runaway Truck Ramp 1 Mile."

options.text: Scrape the car along the guardrail to slow down
options.note: It slows the car, but damages it badly.

options.text: Shift into low gear and pump the brakes
options.note: It slows the car, barely. The player makes it with burnt-out brakes.

options.text: Steer into the runaway truck ramp
options.note: Looks scary (it's a ramp of deep gravel), but it's designed to stop vehicles safely.

options.text: Open the door and jump out
options.note: Jumping from a moving car is deadly.

branches.title: The Uranium Ghost Town
branches.text: Your detour took you off I-70 into an abandoned uranium-mining town in the desert. Old houses, a well, and a rusty sign warning of radiation.

options.text: Drink from the town's well
options.note: Looks like fresh water, but it's likely contaminated with uranium.

options.text: Search the old houses for supplies
options.note: Some useful items, but old mine buildings are unstable.

options.text: Leave immediately
options.note: Safe.

options.text: Fill up from your stored water, not the well
options.note: Old uranium-town wells can be contaminated. The player avoids poison water.

callbacks.title: The Red Mark
callbacks.text: The little girl you agreed to carry west wakes up crying and holding her arm. There's a red, puffy mark on her wrist you didn't notice before.

options.text: Keep her warm and watch her closely
options.note: Fine, but the player stays worried for days.

options.text: Check the mark closely in good light
options.note: It's chilblains, a skin reaction to cold, not a bite. Warm her hands slowly, and she's fine.

options.text: Leave her with strangers at the next stop
options.note: She wasn't infected, and the player broke a promise to her family.

options.text: Rub the mark with snow to calm the swelling
options.note: Looks like first aid, but snow makes cold injuries worse.

callbacks.title: Shivering in the Dark
callbacks.text: Two scenarios after you soaked in the hot springs, you're still shivering hard, your fingers are clumsy, and you're slurring a little. Your companion is worried.

options.text: Keep moving to warm up
options.note: Light movement helps, but pushing hard while confused is dangerous.

options.text: Take a hot shower to warm up fast
options.note: Looks like the fastest fix, but rapid heat can shock the body. Warm up gradually.

options.text: Huddle with your companion under blankets
options.note: It works, but slowly.

options.text: Get into dry clothes and a sleeping bag, and drink something warm and sweet
options.note: These are signs of mild hypothermia. Dry layers and warm sugary drinks are the right treatment.

cities.route: I-80 East: Parleys Canyon > Wyoming > Nebraska > Iowa > south of Chicago > Ohio > Pennsylvania > New Jersey > New York City
cities.profile: Mid-size, well-prepared city. Many Utah families keep emergency food storage, so the player can start well stocked. Wyoming's cold hits on Day 2. The player ends in the most infected city in the game, New York, so the last day is the hardest. Safe zone: Governors Island in New York Harbor.

scenarios.title: Emergency Food Storage
scenarios.text: Salt Lake City is tense. Your neighbor Ruth's basement holds a year of emergency food and water. She offers to share, but the infected just broke into the house across the street.

options.text: Grab her food while she isn't looking
options.note: She notices. The player loses a friend, and the noise draws the infected.

options.text: Take a small share and leave alone
options.note: Enough supplies for a few days, but no ally.

options.text: Help Ruth pack fast and leave together
options.note: The player gains a skilled ally and a trunk full of food and water. Sets NEIGHBOR_ALLY.

options.text: Decline, since you'll find food on the road
options.note: The player starts underprepared.

scenarios.title: Parleys Canyon
scenarios.text: Parleys Canyon is the only interstate east. It's steep, icy and jammed with cars trying to escape. Headlights are flickering out, and car doors are opening.

options.text: Wait in the jam
options.note: The infected work their way through the stalled cars.

options.text: Take a back road through the hills
options.note: Slow and winding, but the player is past the jam by midnight.

options.text: Take a snowcat from a ski resort maintenance yard
options.note: Built for snow and mountains. It drives right around the jam.

options.text: Drive on the shoulder
options.note: Ice and rock walls.

scenarios.title: Frozen Stiff in Laramie
scenarios.text: In Laramie it's -12°F. The infected on the streets are frozen nearly solid. A grocery store sits unguarded across the street, and some houses on the edge of town look untouched.

options.text: Drive through town without stopping
options.note: Safe, but the player misses the best supply run in Wyoming.

options.text: Search the houses on the edge of town
options.note: Some food, but the player scrapes their hand climbing through a broken window. Sets SCRAPED_HAND.

options.text: Poke a frozen infected to see if it's dead
options.note: Looks harmless, but its jaw still works.

options.text: Raid the grocery store quickly while the infected are frozen
options.note: The cold rule from our infection model: below 20°F, the infected slow way down. Use it.

scenarios.title: The University Gym
scenarios.text: Survivors have barricaded the university gym in Laramie. A guard at the door says, "We don't let strangers in after dark." The temperature is falling toward -20°F.

options.text: Sleep in your car in the parking lot
options.note: Cold but safe near the guards.

options.text: Beg for supplies through the door
options.note: They might hand some out. Might not.

options.text: Offer to take a night shift on guard duty
options.note: Work earns trust. A warm cot, hot soup and water after the shift.

options.text: Sneak in through the side door
options.note: Caught and thrown out into -20°F.

scenarios.title: The Crashed Plane
scenarios.text: A small cargo plane has crash-landed in a Nebraska field. Boxes marked with red crosses are scattered across the snow. The cockpit door is cracked open, and something is moving inside.

options.text: Look for survivors near the wreck
options.note: The co-pilot is alive but injured. A tough choice.

options.text: Search the cockpit for the pilot's gear
options.note: The pilot survived the crash, but not the infection.

options.text: Grab the medical supply boxes
options.note: Antibiotics and bandages, the rarest supplies in the game. Sets MED_SUPPLIES.

options.text: Ignore it and drive on
options.note: Safe, but the player misses valuable supplies.

scenarios.title: The Museum Over the Highway
scenarios.text: In Kearney, Nebraska, a museum built as a bridge stretches right over I-80. Survivors inside are lowering a rope ladder. Infected wander the highway below.

options.text: Sleep under the bridge
options.note: The infected wander the highway at night.

options.text: Camp in a Kearney motel parking lot
options.note: Okay, but the motel has broken doors and wanderers.

options.text: Climb the rope ladder and stay with them
options.note: High above the road with one way in. They share dinner.

options.text: Keep driving through the night
options.note: Empty Nebraska roads, where a breakdown means no help.

scenarios.title: The World's Largest Truck Stop
scenarios.text: In Walcott, Iowa, the world's largest truck stop is now a survivor marketplace. Truckers are trading fuel, food and parts out of their trailers. A fight breaks out nearby.

options.text: Search the abandoned trucks at the back of the lot
options.note: Food, but some cabs aren't empty.

options.text: Fuel up and keep driving
options.note: Fine, but the player has no spare tire for the rest of the trip.

options.text: Trade for food and a spare tire, then leave before the fight spreads
options.note: A spare tire saves the player from a blowout later. Sets SPARE_TIRE.

options.text: Try to steal from a trailer during the fight
options.note: Truckers watch each other's backs. Caught.

scenarios.title: Bite Check at the River
scenarios.text: At the Mississippi River bridge into Illinois, soldiers check every traveler for bites. A long line of cars waits in the cold. Someone ahead of you starts to panic.

options.text: Offer the soldiers supplies to skip the line
options.note: Might work. Might get the player searched more closely.

options.text: Find another bridge
options.note: Safe, but it costs half a day.

options.text: Run the checkpoint
options.note: Soldiers open fire, and the player is now wanted at every checkpoint east.

options.text: Wait your turn and show you're clean
options.note: The player passes safely and gets water and a stamped travel pass.

scenarios.title: Fleeing Chicago
scenarios.text: Smoke rises over Chicago. A line of survivors on foot is walking west past your car, carrying everything they own. A woman bangs on your window, begging for water.

options.text: Give her a bottle and ask which roads are clear
options.note: People leaving an area know it best. They point the player to a clear route south of the jam.

options.text: Head into the city to look for supplies
options.note: Chicago is huge and heavily infected.

options.text: Keep driving without stopping
options.note: Fine, but the player drives into the I-80 jam the survivors knew about.

options.text: Offer a family a ride
options.note: A good deed, but more mouths to feed and slower travel.

scenarios.title: Ice Fishing on Lake Erie
scenarios.text: Near Cleveland, Lake Erie is frozen. Survivors are ice fishing near the shore around small heaters. Farther out, the ice is dark and wet.

options.text: Walk farther out on the ice to find your own fishing spot
options.note: Looks productive, but the ice gets thinner farther out.

options.text: Keep driving along the lake
options.note: Fine, but lake-effect snow is building.

options.text: Camp on the shore with them overnight
options.note: A friendly night, but the player loses time in the morning.

options.text: Trade gas for fresh fish and a pot of boiled lake water
options.note: Fresh protein and safe water. They share their weather radio too.

scenarios.title: The Mountain Trooper
scenarios.text: I-80 climbs through Pennsylvania's mountains in falling snow. A state police car blocks the road with its lights flashing. The trooper inside isn't moving.

options.text: Speed past the police car
options.note: Straight onto the collapsed bridge.

options.text: Wait for the plow to clear the road
options.note: Safe, but it costs half a day.

options.text: Stop at a distance, call out, and check before getting close
options.note: He's alive but injured. He warns of a collapsed bridge ahead and shows the detour.

options.text: Run up and open his door
options.note: He's alive, but the player got lucky.

scenarios.title: Suburban Fences
scenarios.text: The New Jersey suburbs are quiet. Too quiet. A shopping mall glows nearby, and a house with a tall fence sits on a dead-end street.

options.text: Sleep in the house with the tall fence
options.note: Fences slow the infected, and the water heater tank holds 40 gallons of drinkable water.

options.text: Sleep in the mall
options.note: Looks like it has everything, but malls draw crowds and the infected.

options.text: Sleep in your car on the dead-end street
options.note: Fine, but there's no fence.

options.text: Search the mall food court before bed
options.note: Good food, but the player is inside a dark mall at night.

scenarios.title: The Harbor Crossing
scenarios.text: At dawn you reach the Bayonne pier, take a small boat and head for Governors Island. Halfway across, the engine sputters and dies. The current pushes you toward Manhattan.

options.text: Row steadily toward the island
options.note: Slow but steady. Patrol boats spot the player and tow them in.

options.text: Wave a bright shirt to signal for help
options.note: It works eventually, but the player drifts for an hour.

options.text: Jump in and swim
options.note: 38°F water. Hypothermia in minutes.

options.text: Try to restart the engine over and over
options.note: Looks like the fix, but it floods the engine while the current pulls the boat away.

scenarios.title: Governors Island Dock
scenarios.text: You reach the Governors Island safe zone dock. Guards tell you everyone must be quarantined for 24 hours before entering.

options.text: Accept the quarantine
options.note: Safety rules keep the island infection-free. Victory.

options.text: Wait on the dock until the guards change shifts
options.note: The next guard says the same thing. Time wasted.

options.text: Refuse quarantine and demand entry
options.note: The player is turned away.

options.text: Argue that you've traveled 1,968 miles
options.note: The guards respect it but follow the rules.

branches.title: Breakdown in the Middle of Nowhere
branches.text: Your bad choice has left your car dead on an empty stretch of highway, 40 miles from the nearest town. It's -15°F, and the wind is picking up.

options.text: Bundle up in every layer and wait
options.note: It works, but it's a miserable, freezing night.

options.text: Signal passing traffic with your flashlight
options.note: Could bring help. Could bring raiders.

options.text: Stay with the car, burn a candle in a coffee can for heat, and crack a window
options.note: A candle can raise a closed car's temperature a few degrees. Cracking a window prevents fumes. Staying with the car means rescuers can find the player.

options.text: Walk 40 miles to town
options.note: Looks like taking charge, but 40 miles at -15°F means death from cold.

branches.title: The Wild Horse Wranglers
branches.text: Your risky choice put you face to face with federal wild-horse wranglers on horseback in the Red Desert. They offer to lead you across an old ranch road.

options.text: Follow the wranglers across the ranch road
options.note: They know the land. The road bypasses a jam on I-80.

options.text: Ask them to sell you a horse
options.note: They might, but horses need care and food the player doesn't have.

options.text: Thank them and stay on I-80
options.note: Safe.

options.text: Try to take one of their horses
options.note: They outnumber the player and know horses.

branches.title: Spike Strip Ambush
branches.text: Your bad choice led you onto a quiet stretch of highway where raiders laid a spike strip. Your front tire is flat, and you see figures walking toward you.

options.text: Lock the doors and honk to draw them off
options.note: The noise attracts infected, which scatter the raiders, but now the player is surrounded by infected.

options.text: Change to your spare tire fast and leave
options.note: Code note: needs the SPARE_TIRE flag from the World's Largest Truck Stop (SLC 8 M, Best option). Without it, show the alternate option.

alt.text: Drive slowly on the flat tire to escape
alt.note: No spare. Driving on a flat ruins the rim, but the player escapes.

options.text: Run on foot into the woods
options.note: Safe from the raiders, but the player loses the car.

options.text: Get out and talk to the raiders
options.note: They take everything.

branches.title: The Old Steam Train
branches.text: Your gamble put you in Jim Thorpe, PA, a mountain town with an old tourist steam train. Its crew says they can run it east to the Delaware River.

options.text: Thank them and drive on
options.note: Safe.

options.text: Try to steer the train yourself
options.note: The player has no idea how to run a steam engine.

options.text: Ride the steam train east
options.note: Tracks avoid the jammed interstate. A fast, safe ride.

options.text: Help them shovel coal for a ride
options.note: It works, but it's hard work and the player is exhausted.

callbacks.title: Ruth's Ankle
callbacks.text: Ruth, your neighbor from Salt Lake City, slips on ice getting out of the car. Her ankle swells fast, and she can't put weight on it.

options.text: Pull and twist her foot to "pop it back in place"
options.note: Looks like quick first aid, but untrained people can make a sprain or break much worse.

options.text: Wrap the ankle, raise it, and pack snow in a cloth on it for 15 minutes
options.note: Rest, compression, elevation and cold reduce the swelling. She can limp by morning.

options.text: Leave her and keep going
options.note: She's an ally with food and skills. Abandoning her is a huge story penalty.

options.text: Help her into the back seat and keep going
options.note: Fine, but she'll be slow for days.

callbacks.title: The Hot, Swollen Hand
callbacks.text: The hand you scraped climbing through a window in Laramie is now hot, swollen, and red. A red line is starting to creep up your wrist.

options.text: Clean it and take antibiotics from the crashed plane's medical boxes
options.note: Code note: needs the MED_SUPPLIES flag (SLC 6 M, Best option). A red line spreading from a wound is a serious bacterial infection, and antibiotics are the right fix.

alt.text: Clean it, keep it raised, and look for a pharmacy
alt.note: Without antibiotics, the player has to hope for a pharmacy soon.

options.text: Soak it in warm salt water
options.note: Helps a little, but it isn't enough on its own.

options.text: Cut the wound open to "let the infection out"
options.note: Looks like doing something, but it can spread the infection.

options.text: Ignore it. It's not a bite
options.note: True, it's not a bite, but a spreading infection can still be deadly.

cities.route: Jackson, WY > Hoback Canyon > I-80 at Rock Springs > Nebraska > Omaha > Iowa > Chicago > I-90 along Lake Erie > Buffalo > New York Thruway > Mass Pike > Boston
cities.profile: The smallest and coldest start (about 15°F). The deep cold slows the infected, but a small town has nowhere to hide. Early game: mountains, elk and snowmobiles. Late game: lake-effect snow and a crowded Northeast. Safe zone: Fort Warren on Georges Island in Boston Harbor.

scenarios.title: The Antler Arches
scenarios.text: Jackson's town square, under its famous elk-antler arches, is chaos. The only roads out are mountain passes. The sheriff is shouting through a megaphone as infected stumble out of a ski shop.

options.text: Grab food from your pantry and shelter at home
options.note: Supplies help, but in a small town the infection reaches everyone.

options.text: Ride the ski resort tram up to scout
options.note: A great view, but if the power fails the player is stuck up top.

options.text: Run to the sheriff and offer your help
options.note: Locals trust locals. He tells the player Hoback Canyon is still open and hands them water.

options.text: Drive over Teton Pass to the west
options.note: Steep, icy, avalanche country in winter. Closed and deadly.

scenarios.title: The Elk Refuge
scenarios.text: Thousands of elk crowd the snowy refuge outside town. Infected are coming down the road behind you, and the herd blocks the only way south.

options.text: Hide at the refuge visitor center
options.note: Safe for the night, with a vending machine.

options.text: Turn back to town for more supplies
options.note: The infected are in town now.

options.text: Drive slowly through the middle of the herd
options.note: Looks dangerous, but the elk form a living wall that slows the infected. An antler scrapes the grille. Sets ELK_DAMAGE.

options.text: Honk and scatter the elk
options.note: The stampede damages the car, and the noise draws the infected.

scenarios.title: Hoback Canyon
scenarios.text: Hoback Canyon is narrow and icy. A rancher's snowmobile trailer sits at a pullout. The rancher is slumped over the steering wheel of his truck.

options.text: Leave your car and ride the snowmobile out
options.note: Not enough range or storage for a cross-country trip.

options.text: Hook the snowmobile trailer to your car and go
options.note: Backup transport for deep snow later. Smart thinking ahead. Sets SNOWMOBILE.

options.text: Check on the rancher
options.note: He's turned. The player grabs his cooler but takes a risk.

options.text: Keep driving slowly through the canyon
options.note: Safe, but no backup for the deep snow ahead.

scenarios.title: The Overrun Truck Stop
scenarios.text: You reach I-80 at Rock Springs. The truck stop's shelves are full of food and drinks, but its doors are smeared with blood and the lights flicker inside.

options.text: Skip the store and siphon gas from cars on the off-ramp
options.note: Avoid the crowd. Fuel is still within reach.

options.text: Grab drinks from the outdoor coolers by the pumps
options.note: Water is right there, but the infected are 50 feet away.

options.text: Coast on to the next town
options.note: Okay for now, but it's 100 empty miles.

options.text: Run in for the food and drinks
options.note: Looks like a supply jackpot, but it's overrun.

scenarios.title: The Crop Duster
scenarios.text: In the Nebraska Panhandle, a crop-dusting plane sits in a snowy field. The pilot waves you down. He's scouting from the air and knows where the roads are blocked.

options.text: Wave and drive on
options.note: Fine, but the player drives toward a blocked road he could have warned them about.

options.text: Ask him to fly you east
options.note: His fuel only reaches 200 miles, and the player's car stays behind.

options.text: Ask the pilot to scout your route and share what he knows
options.note: Aerial intel shows the player which roads are clear. He promises to warn them if anything changes. Sets PILOT_INTEL.

options.text: Try to take the plane
options.note: The pilot fights back.

scenarios.title: The Omaha Crossing
scenarios.text: At Omaha, the Missouri River bridge into Iowa has a military checkpoint with floodlights. A soldier yells, "Last crossing tonight! Bridge closes at midnight!"

options.text: Sleep in your car and cross in the morning
options.note: The bridge is closed by morning, and the player loses a day.

options.text: Get in line and cross tonight
options.note: The player crosses before the bridge closes, and soldiers hand out ration packs.

options.text: Argue with the soldiers about the long line
options.note: Pushing makes them suspicious, and the player only just gets through.

options.text: Drive back into Omaha to find another bridge
options.note: The city is infected, and the other bridges are closed too.

scenarios.title: Iowa Blizzard
scenarios.text: A blizzard sweeps across Iowa. Snow blows sideways and the highway disappears. A red barn is barely visible, and something is moving in the white behind you.

options.text: Keep driving in the whiteout
options.note: The player drives off the road into a snowy ditch.

options.text: Unhook the snowmobile and keep going
options.note: Fast in snow, but the player could get lost in a whiteout.

alt.text: Follow a snowplow's tracks through the storm
alt.note: No snowmobile. The plow tracks fill in fast, and the player could lose the trail.

options.text: Pull into the barn and wait out the storm
options.note: Out of the wind, with hay for insulation and a farmhouse well.

options.text: Stop on the shoulder with the hazard lights on
options.note: Survivable, but trucks might hit the car.

scenarios.title: The Lighthouse Keeper
scenarios.text: Near Chicago, on the shore of Lake Michigan, a lighthouse keeper's house is lit by candles. The keeper is waving a lantern from the doorway. Behind you, Chicago is burning.

options.text: Drive the lakefront road toward Indiana
options.note: Night roads near a burning city.

options.text: Go to the keeper and ask for shelter
options.note: He's friendly, and he has canned food and rain barrels of water.

options.text: Sleep in your car by the lighthouse
options.note: Fine, but cold wind off the lake.

options.text: Climb the lighthouse in the dark to see the city
options.note: Icy steps and no light.

scenarios.title: Lake-Effect Whiteout
scenarios.text: Near Toledo, lake-effect snow off Lake Erie is dumping two inches an hour. A plow truck is ahead of you. A car in the ditch beside you has its door hanging open.

options.text: Check the car in the ditch
options.note: A bag of groceries, and the owner nearby. Not a pleasant surprise.

options.text: Follow the plow at a safe distance
options.note: It clears the road, and its flashing lights guide the player.

options.text: Pull over and wait
options.note: Time lost, but safe.

options.text: Pass the plow to go faster
options.note: Into unplowed snow. Stuck.

scenarios.title: The Rock Museum
scenarios.text: In Cleveland, the glass pyramid of a famous rock and roll museum sits on the lakefront. Survivors are playing guitars inside, and the smell of cooking drifts out.

options.text: Camp outside the city
options.note: Fine, but cold.

options.text: Knock and introduce yourself
options.note: Friendly musicians. A warm meal, water and a morale boost.

options.text: Break in through the glass
options.note: Loud, and the survivors defend themselves.

options.text: Drive through the city at night
options.note: Infected in the streets.

scenarios.title: Four Feet of Snow
scenarios.text: Overnight, Erie, Pennsylvania, got four feet of lake-effect snow. Your car is buried. Shapes are stumbling through the drifts toward you.

options.text: Unhook the snowmobile you towed from Wyoming
options.note: Looks like a gamble, but it's built for this. The player rides to the next plowed town.

alt.text: Grab a snowblower from the hardware store across the street
alt.note: No snowmobile. A snowblower clears a path to the plowed road in an hour.

options.text: Walk to town for help
options.note: Four feet of snow on foot.

options.text: Try to drive the car out
options.note: Stuck. The car isn't going anywhere.

options.text: Dig out by hand
options.note: Hours of shoveling, and the player is exhausted.

scenarios.title: Buffalo
scenarios.text: Buffalo's survivors have gathered in the football stadium and are broadcasting an invitation on the radio. Across the road, a wing restaurant has a walk-in freezer.

options.text: Go to the stadium
options.note: Looks safe with all those people, but crowds turn into outbreaks.

options.text: Shelter in the wing restaurant and raid the freezer
options.note: Small, lockable and full of frozen food. Snow melted on the grill gives water.

options.text: Sleep in your car
options.note: Fine, but the car is half-buried in snow.

options.text: Drive on to Rochester
options.note: Snowy night roads.

scenarios.title: The Harbor Route
scenarios.text: The Mass Pike into Boston is jammed. The radio says the safe zone is Fort Warren on Georges Island, and the last boats leave from the harbor tonight.

options.text: Leave the car and walk the commuter rail tracks into the city
options.note: The tracks are clear of jammed cars and lead straight toward the harbor.

options.text: Use your snowmobile on the frozen river into the city
options.note: Fast, but the river ice is thin near the harbor.

alt.text: Walk the frozen river path into the city
alt.note: No snowmobile. Walking the riverbank is slow and exposed, and the ice near the harbor is thin.

options.text: Wait in the suburbs for the jam to clear
options.note: Time lost, and the boat runs end tonight.

options.text: Drive into downtown Boston
options.note: Jammed streets full of the infected.

scenarios.title: The Last Boat
scenarios.text: At the harbor, the last boat to Fort Warren is about to leave before the water freezes tonight. There's one seat left, and an injured nurse also needs it.

options.text: Fight the nurse for the seat
options.note: The captain refuses to take either of you.

options.text: Suggest you both squeeze in and leave your heavy gear behind
options.note: Boats are limited by weight, not seats. Leaving the gear makes room for both. Victory.

options.text: Offer the captain fuel to make an extra trip
options.note: He might agree, but the harbor is freezing fast.

options.text: Give the nurse your seat and wait for a morning boat
options.note: The morning boat comes, and the player makes it a day late.

branches.title: Avalanche in Hoback Canyon
branches.text: Your bad choice left you in Hoback Canyon when a small avalanche buries the road ahead of you. A second slope above you is cracking.

options.text: Get out and dig through the snow ahead
options.note: Looks like progress, but the player is standing in the slide path when the second slope lets go.

options.text: Stay put in the car and wait
options.note: The car is a shell, but if the second slope slides, the player is buried.

options.text: Drive over the snow pile
options.note: Possible with four-wheel drive, but the car could get stuck in the path.

options.text: Back up quickly to the last wide pullout and wait for the slope to settle
options.note: Get out of the slide path first. Avalanche terrain needs patience.

branches.title: The South Pass Ghost Town
branches.text: Your detour took you to an old mining ghost town on the Oregon Trail. A hermit lives in one restored cabin with a wood stove and stacks of firewood.

options.text: Explore the old mine for supplies
options.note: Old mines can collapse.

options.text: Raid his woodpile while he sleeps
options.note: He's a light sleeper with a rifle.

options.text: Sleep in another empty cabin
options.note: Cold, but the player has a roof.

options.text: Knock and offer to chop wood for a night by the stove
options.note: The hermit knows the backcountry and shows the player a shortcut to I-80.

branches.title: Stuck on Lake Erie Shore Ice
branches.text: Your bad choice put your car sliding off a lakeside road onto the frozen shoreline of Lake Erie. The ice is cracking under the front tires.

options.text: Get out the back, slowly crawl to shore, and leave the car
options.note: Spread the body's weight and get off the ice. Cars can be replaced.

options.text: Gun the engine to back off the ice
options.note: Looks like the way to save the car, but the vibration cracks the ice faster.

options.text: Grab your bag and walk carefully to shore
options.note: Faster, but standing puts more weight on thin ice.

options.text: Tie a rope to a tree and try to pull the car back
options.note: Clever, but slow, and the ice keeps cracking.

branches.title: The Root Cellar
branches.text: Your gamble led you off the highway to a farm off the highway. The family keeps a stone root cellar full of potatoes, apples, and canned food, and they're worried about raiders.

options.text: Offer to take them east with you
options.note: A big group, slower, but stronger.

options.text: Offer to stand guard tonight for a share of food
options.note: They need help. The player gets food and a safe night.

options.text: Lock them out of their own root cellar
options.note: They're desperate and armed.

options.text: Buy a sack of potatoes and keep going
options.note: Fine.

callbacks.title: Antler in the Grille
callbacks.text: Two scenarios after you crept through the elk herd, steam pours from your hood. An elk antler punctured the grille and radiator, and the engine is overheating.

options.text: Swap the radiator from an abandoned car
options.note: Doable, but it takes hours and tools.

options.text: Pour pepper from the snack bag into the radiator to plug the small hole, then top it off with melted snow
options.note: A real old-school roadside trick. Pepper grains plug small radiator leaks for a while.

options.text: Keep driving until the engine overheats completely
options.note: The engine seizes. No more car.

options.text: Stop every 20 miles to add melted snow
options.note: It works, but it's very slow.

callbacks.title: A Message from the Sky
callbacks.text: The crop-duster pilot you met flies low over your car, wagging his wings. A bottle with a note drops into the snow nearby: "Omaha bridge closes tomorrow. Cross TONIGHT."

options.text: Ignore it. Pilots don't know roads
options.note: The bridge closes, and the player loses a day.

options.text: Follow his advice and cross tonight
options.note: The player gets across before the closure.

options.text: Try to signal the pilot back for more info
options.note: He's already gone, and it wastes time.

options.text: Cross first thing in the morning
options.note: Close call. The player just makes it.

cities.route: I-90 East: Snoqualmie Pass > Spokane > Montana > Wyoming > Black Hills > South Dakota > Wisconsin > Chicago > Indianapolis > Cincinnati
cities.profile: A mild, rainy start (41°F) means slower early spread. The player leaves a wet city and drives straight into the coldest country in the game: Montana and the Dakotas. Skipping winter gear on Day 2 hurts. Safe zone: Cincinnati's fortified riverfront.

scenarios.title: Rain and Ferries
scenarios.text: It's a gray, rainy morning in Seattle. Alarms sound downtown. The ferry terminal is packed with screaming people, and I-90 east toward the mountains is still moving.

options.text: Stock up at a grocery store first, then drive east
options.note: Food and water for days, but the lines are long and tense.

options.text: Drive east on I-90 toward the mountains right now
options.note: Leave before the roads clog. Mild weather makes the early escape easier.

options.text: Ride the monorail downtown to look for your friend
options.note: Loyal, but the player is now in the city center.

options.text: Crowd onto a ferry to the islands
options.note: Islands sound safe, but a packed ferry spreads infection, and there's no escape from the boat.

scenarios.title: Snoqualmie Pass
scenarios.text: The rain turns to heavy snow as you climb Snoqualmie Pass. Signs flash "Chains Required." A car spins out ahead of you and slams into the guardrail.

options.text: Check on the car that crashed
options.note: The driver is hurt, and maybe more than hurt.

options.text: Sleep at the ski area lodge at the summit
options.note: Warm, with a snack bar, but crowded with travelers.

options.text: Ignore the signs and keep driving
options.note: The car slides off the steep grade.

options.text: Pull over and put chains on before going any higher
options.note: Required by law and life-saving on the pass.

scenarios.title: Spokane Gear Store
scenarios.text: Spokane's streets are quiet. A big outdoor-gear store sits near the highway with its doors wide open. Montana is next, and you're dressed for Seattle rain.

options.text: Grab snacks and water only
options.note: Partial prep. The player will regret it in Montana. Sets NO_WINTER_GEAR.

options.text: Skip the gear, since you'll be in the car
options.note: If the car breaks down, rain jackets mean frostbite. Sets NO_WINTER_GEAR.

options.text: Check the hospital next door for medicine
options.note: Medicine is there, but so are the infected.

options.text: Get real winter gear: parka, boots and gloves
options.note: Montana and the Dakotas will be far colder. Gear up now.

scenarios.title: The Toxic Lake
scenarios.text: Near Butte, Montana, an old open-pit mine has filled with a red lake. Your water is almost gone. A mine office nearby has a light on.

options.text: Fill your water jugs from the lake
options.note: Water is water? No. It's toxic mine water that will poison the player.

options.text: Check the mine office, which has a generator and a water cooler
options.note: Warm, locked and safe, with clean drinking water.

options.text: Camp outside town and melt snow for water
options.note: Works, but slowly.

options.text: Search the old mine buildings for supplies
options.note: Unstable buildings and possibly bad air.

scenarios.title: The Continental Divide
scenarios.text: Homestake Pass crosses the Continental Divide. It's -10°F. Your engine sputters. The fuel line is freezing, and the infected are walking up the road behind you.

options.text: Coast the car downhill to restart it
options.note: Risky on an icy mountain grade.

options.text: Idle the engine to warm the fuel line
options.note: Works slowly, and burns fuel.

options.text: Keep driving and hope it clears
options.note: The engine dies on the pass.

options.text: Add fuel-line antifreeze from the gas station at the top
options.note: A real winter trick that keeps fuel flowing.

scenarios.title: Refinery Glow
scenarios.text: In Billings, an oil refinery glows on the horizon. Armed workers guard the gates. The smell of food drifts from their camp kitchen.

options.text: Skip it and use what you have
options.note: Okay for now, but the empty plains are ahead.

options.text: Ask to stay inside the refinery overnight
options.note: Safe walls, but they'll want the player to work a shift.

options.text: Offer to trade a skill (fixing, cooking, guarding) for food and fuel
options.note: They need help more than supplies. A full tank and a hot meal.

options.text: Sneak through the fence to fill up
options.note: Guards with floodlights. Shots fired.

scenarios.title: The Tower
scenarios.text: Devils Tower, a giant rock column, rises from the snowy plains. A group of stranded rock climbers is camped at its base, and infected are circling their camp.

options.text: Climb the tower for a lookout point
options.note: Looks like a smart scouting move, but it's icy rock and the player has no training.
